extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers of philosophy and literary aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts normative criteria the two essays advance for (1) what counts as genuine loyalty and as a worthy cause, and (2) what counts as poetic value and how poetry should be judged. Useful for assessing moral-philosophical commitments and aesthetic judgments in essays or criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Loyalty is 'the thorough-going and practical devotion of a self to a cause.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loyalty is not a mere glow of enthusiasm; it involves deeds as well as emotions. The devotedness must be practical and voluntary; loyalty is 'an affair of his deeds as well as of his emotions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Central characteristic: cause conceived as a reality
rubrics_metrics.description: The loyal spirit 'conceives and values its cause as a reality, as an object that has a being of its own,' a type of reality different from physical things or natural laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A genuine cause for loyalty is treated as essentially spiritual; if such causes are real, then reality contains beings and laws superior in type to mere natural mechanism. This is central to the loyal outlook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes are super-personal unities, not mere aggregates
rubrics_metrics.description: Causes are neither merely detached individuals nor mere crowds; they are personal and 'super-personal'—unities or common lives that are more than the sum of individual members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: true friendship as a 'common life' or 'united personality'; a country as an 'invisible but... perfectly real spiritual unity' rather than merely the aggregate of citizens or offices. You cannot be truly loyal to a crowd merely as a crowd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical fruitfulness as criterion of religious loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious faith that is a genuine loyalty must 'bear fruit in works' rather than be solely mystic ecstasy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religion in a higher sense involves practical relation and service to a spiritual world; 'loyalty is essentially adoration with service, and that there is no true adoration without practical loyalty.' Thus evaluate religious claims by their practical, moral outcomes as well as interior insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality of loyalty to metaphysical commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Loyalty as a doctrine is 'neutral as to every so-called conflict between science and religion'—it is founded on man's inner needs rather than metaphysical decisions about nature's mechanism or miracles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One can practice loyalty without deciding whether nature is mechanistic or whether gods exist; loyalty focuses on devotion to a cause and on human moral functioning rather than first settling metaphysical questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlargement and universality of loyalty without loss of concreteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Loyalty can 'constantly enlarge its scope' and 'become universally human in its interests without losing its concreteness'—special duties can be restated in terms of a duly generalized spirit of loyalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A loyal life balances fidelity to a particular cause (family, vocation) with an enlightened sense of kinship to all loyal persons; moral conflicts are to be resolved via the principle of loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science as a form of loyalty (criterion for scientific validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study of natural science is 'a very beautiful and humane expression of a certain exalted form of loyalty'—the loyalty to the cause of enlarging and unifying human experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific knowledge presupposes that human observations can be revised, synthesized, and unified into a common realm of experience. The possibility and validity of science depend on this unity; if human experience were only isolated private fancies, science would be merely metaphor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion of unity for claims about reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Either sciences give progressive insight into truth (implying a real unity of human experience and an over-individual reality), or none of science or loyalty is more than myth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claims about reality by their capacity to participate in and be confirmed by the synthesized, shared human experience; the coherence and communal validation of observations is what gives scientific claims real status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty as source of rational religious insight free from superstition
rubrics_metrics.description: Growing in loyalty provides 'the deepset source of a genuinely significant religious insight' that is free from superstition because it ties spiritual insight to practical devotion and the enlarged unity of human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious insight can be obtained by 'reasonable means' insofar as loyalty helps one apprehend a unifying spiritual reality; the essay urges keeping religion practical and critical rather than reverting to magical superstition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of genuine objectivity (self-refuting skepticism rejected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total skepticism is self-refuting; the rational view depends on maintaining that the loyal's object (their cause) is 'indeed... a type of reality which rationally survives all criticisms and underlies all doubts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate extreme skeptical positions by whether they undermine the very conditions that make science and loyalty intelligible; a philosophical position that denies the unity of experience collapses its own pretensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's intrinsic (poetic) value
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry's experience is 'an end in itself' and has intrinsic value; 'its poetic value is this intrinsic worth alone' and must be judged 'entirely from within.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poem is to be evaluated primarily by the imaginative experience it gives (sounds, images, thoughts, emotions), not by external moral, instructive, or utilitarian effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ulterior ends tend to lower poetic value
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of ulterior ends (culture, religion, instruction, patriotism, fame, money) 'tends to lower poetic value' because it takes poetry out of its proper atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bradley gives anti-examples: judging poems by their instruction or patriotic effect can lead to absurd comparisons (e.g., if poetic value were instruction, a didactic health manual might be prized). Thus avoid assessing poetry chiefly by external purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as autonomous world and necessity of metrical form
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is 'a world by itself, independent, complete, autonomous'; include metrical form as part of the essence of poetry—not a mere accident or vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poem is 'the succession of experiences—sounds, images, thoughts, emotions—through which we pass' when reading poetically. Therefore evaluation must attend to formal features (meter, sound) as integral to poetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's relation to life: analogy, not identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry and life are different forms of the same thing; poetry is not life nor a copy of it but an analogue with a different kind of existence, appealing to contemplative imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of poetry should recognize that poetic satisfaction comes from a contemplative imaginative experience 'saturated with the results of "real" experience' but not identical to the pragmatic, situated concerns of life.
